correctness.rationale: A first-coordinate coincidence is transverse: uniqueness prohibits both differences from vanishing, and the inhibitory secant across the distinct second coordinates is strictly positive even if the pointwise derivative can vanish. Remove the common decay and scale by sqrt(B), sqrt(A). The lifted phase satisfies θ′=d cos²θ+c sin²θ+δ sin(2θ)≤Ω+δ sin(2θ), with c,d∈[0,Ω]. Every vertical hit is upward. Thus the next hit must advance by π even if phase reverses away from the vertical. If |δ|<Ω, integrating the reciprocal of the positive upper field over one period gives π/sqrt(Ω²−δ²), using the tangent substitution; the transformed phase has derivative ≤1 without any assumption of monotone rotation. If |δ|≥Ω the comparison flow cannot reach the next vertical ray because a stationary angle lies strictly between, including at the critical double zero. The bounded response construction joins the affine core to tails with matching slopes and has a stable linear core. Boundedness of the associated matrix semigroup keeps sufficiently small perturbations in that core for all forward times; the sine in the first-coordinate difference gives consecutive equality times exactly the claimed distance apart.
residual_risks: The script uses deterministic sinusoidal modulation, despite the word ‘randomly’ in the frozen verification prose. These optional finite checks are not certificates of the variable-secant or infinite-time result.
Strict inhibition rules out exactly flat intervals; the limitation concerning noise should be understood as allowing arbitrarily weak secants, not assuming intervals of literal constancy.
